description: The optimisation theory and algorithms that train machine learning models: convex sets and functions, gradient descent and its convergence, stochastic and mini-batch methods, momentum and adaptive methods such as Adam, constrained optimisation with Lagrange multipliers and duality, second-order and quasi-Newton methods, and the practice of tuning and diagnosing training. Every algorithm is derived, implemented from scratch and watched moving across loss surfaces in the browser before it is used on real models.
modelledOn: Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning (optimisation chapters)
outcomes: Formulate learning problems as optimisation problems and recognise when they are convex.
Prove and apply the convergence properties of gradient descent under smoothness and strong convexity.
Implement stochastic, mini-batch, momentum and adaptive methods and explain their trade-offs in noise, speed and memory.
Solve constrained problems with Lagrange multipliers, KKT conditions and duality, including the support vector machine.
Apply Newton, quasi-Newton and other second-order methods and judge when their cost is justified.
Diagnose and tune training in practice using learning-rate schedules, gradient checks and loss curves.

units.title: Optimisation problems in machine learning
topics: Empirical risk minimisation as an optimisation problem; loss functions and regularisers
Calculus refresher: gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, directional derivatives and Taylor expansions
Local and global minima, saddle points; first- and second-order optimality conditions
Visualising loss surfaces and level sets for linear regression, logistic regression and small networks

units.title: Convex sets and functions
topics: Convex sets: hyperplanes, half-spaces, balls, polyhedra and cones; operations that preserve convexity
Convex functions: definitions, first- and second-order conditions, Jensen's inequality
Operations that preserve convexity; common convex losses in machine learning
Strong convexity, Lipschitz continuity and smoothness; condition number of a problem
Subgradients and non-smooth convex functions such as the L1 norm and hinge loss
Convex problem classes: least squares, linear and quadratic programming

units.title: Gradient descent and its variants
topics: Gradient descent derived from a quadratic upper bound; step size choice
Convergence rates for smooth convex and strongly convex functions
Line search: exact, backtracking and the Armijo and Wolfe conditions
Ill-conditioning, zig-zagging and the role of feature scaling and preconditioning
Subgradient methods, proximal gradient descent and ISTA for lasso
Coordinate descent

units.title: Stochastic optimisation
topics: Stochastic gradient descent: unbiased gradient estimates and their variance
Mini-batches, sampling with and without replacement, epochs and shuffling
Convergence of SGD with decreasing step sizes; the noise ball
Variance reduction: SVRG and SAGA
Generalisation and the implicit regularisation of SGD; large-batch training
Training on a laptop with limited memory: streaming data and small batches

units.title: Momentum and adaptive methods
topics: Heavy-ball momentum and Nesterov accelerated gradient; optimal rates for first-order methods
Adaptive learning rates: AdaGrad, RMSProp and Adam; bias correction
AdamW and decoupled weight decay; when adaptive methods generalise worse
Comparing optimisers on the same problem and reading their trajectories

units.title: Constrained optimisation and Lagrange multipliers
topics: Equality constraints and Lagrange multipliers; geometric interpretation
Inequality constraints and the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions
Lagrangian duality: the dual function, weak and strong duality, Slater's condition
The support vector machine as a quadratic program; the dual and the kernel trick
Projected gradient descent, penalty and barrier methods; an overview of interior-point methods
Allocating a fertiliser budget across farms as a constrained problem

units.title: Second-order methods
topics: Newton's method: derivation, quadratic convergence and damped Newton
Gauss-Newton and Levenberg-Marquardt for least squares; iteratively reweighted least squares for logistic regression
Quasi-Newton methods: BFGS and limited-memory L-BFGS
Hessian-vector products, conjugate gradient and Hessian-free optimisation
Cost and memory of second-order methods at scale

units.title: Optimisation in practice: tuning and diagnostics
topics: Non-convex optimisation in deep learning: saddle points, plateaus and the loss landscape
Learning-rate schedules: step decay, cosine annealing, warm-up and the learning-rate range test
Initialisation, normalisation and gradient clipping; vanishing and exploding gradients
Diagnostics: gradient checking, loss curves, divergence and NaNs; reproducibility and random seeds
Hyperparameter optimisation: grid, random, Bayesian optimisation and early stopping
Capstone: implementing and benchmarking optimisers on a real model with a written analysis
